claim: Recent pertussis resurgence in numerous countries may be driven by asymptomatic infections.
source: Recent pertussis resurgence in numerous countries may be driven by asymptomatic infections.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential driver of pertussis resurgence, presented as a hypothesis in the abstract.

claim: Most pertussis surveillance studies are cross-sectional and cannot distinguish asymptomatic from pre-symptomatic infections.
source: Most pertussis surveillance studies are cross-sectional and cannot distinguish asymptomatic from pre-symptomatic infections.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of existing surveillance methods, based on established knowledge of study designs.

claim: The analysis included 17,442 nasopharyngeal samples from a longitudinal cohort of 1320 Zambian mother/infant pairs.
source: Here we analyze 17,442 nasopharyngeal samples from a longitudinal cohort of 1320 Zambian mother/infant pairs.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and supported by data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: The full range of IS481 qPCR CT values provides insight into pertussis epidemiology.
source: First, we demonstrate that the full range of IS481 qPCR CT values provides insight into pertussis epidemiology, showing concordance of low and high CT results over time, within mother/infant pairs, and in relation to symptomatology.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple analyses presented in the manuscript showing temporal correlation, within-pair concordance, and symptom associations.

claim: There is concordance of low and high CT results over time.
source: showing concordance of low and high CT results over time, within mother/infant pairs, and in relation to symptomatology.
evidence: This is supported by Figure 3B and Figure 4 showing temporal correlation among CT strata.

claim: There is concordance of low and high CT results within mother/infant pairs.
source: showing concordance of low and high CT results over time, within mother/infant pairs, and in relation to symptomatology.
evidence: This is supported by Figure 7D showing strong association of EFI within mother/infant pairs.

claim: There is concordance of low and high CT results in relation to symptomatology.
source: showing concordance of low and high CT results over time, within mother/infant pairs, and in relation to symptomatology.
evidence: This is supported by Figure 8 and Table 4 showing association between EFI and symptoms.

claim: There is a high incidence of asymptomatic pertussis in this population, including among infants.
source: Second, we exploit these full-range qPCR data to demonstrate a high incidence of asymptomatic pertussis, including among infants.
evidence: This is supported by Table 4 showing that 41/177 (23%) of infants with strong EFI were asymptomatic.

claim: The burden of pertussis infection in this population is wider than anticipated.
source: Our results demonstrate a wider burden of pertussis infection than we anticipated in this population, and expose key limitations of threshold-based interpretation of qPCR results in infectious disease surveillance.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing high rates of detection when using full-range CT values compared to traditional thresholds.

claim: Threshold-based interpretation of qPCR results has key limitations in infectious disease surveillance.
source: Our results demonstrate a wider burden of pertussis infection than we anticipated in this population, and expose key limitations of threshold-based interpretation of qPCR results in infectious disease surveillance.
evidence: This is inferred from the analysis showing that many epidemiologically relevant signals would be missed using traditional CT<35 threshold.

claim: Bordetella pertussis remains a significant cause of morbidity and mortality among infants and young children around the world.
source: Bordetella pertussis remains a significant cause of morbidity and mortality among infants and young children around the world (Yeung et al., 2017; Rohani and Scarpino, 2019)
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Pertussis has experienced a resurgence in numerous countries despite long-standing vaccination programs.
source: and has experienced a resurgence in numerous countries despite long-standing vaccination programs (Jackson and Rohani, 2014; He and Mertsola, 2008; Domenech de Cellès et al., 2016; Rohani and Drake, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Transmission by asymptomatic individuals is a suspected driver of pertussis resurgence.
source: Transmission by asymptomatic individuals is a suspected driver of pertussis resurgence (Althouse and Scarpino, 2015; Cherry, 2013)
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature presenting this hypothesis.

claim: Unequivocal evidence documenting asymptomatic infections in adults and children is lacking.
source: though unequivocal evidence documenting asymptomatic infections in adults and children is lacking.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the literature, based on knowledge of existing studies.

claim: Quantitative PCR has supplanted microbiologic culture as the preferred tool for detecting pertussis.
source: Rapid and reliable molecular diagnosis of pertussis is now possible using quantitative PCR (qPCR), which has supplanted microbiologic culture as the preferred tool for detecting pertussis (Vincart et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: Most pertussis surveillance uses cross-sectional monitoring that only captures a single point in time.
source: Yet most pertussis surveillance uses cross-sectional monitoring that only captures a single point in time and thus cannot distinguish asymptomatic from pre-symptomatic infections.
evidence: This is a statement about current surveillance practices based on knowledge of the field.

claim: Cross-sectional monitoring cannot distinguish asymptomatic from pre-symptomatic infections.
source: Yet most pertussis surveillance uses cross-sectional monitoring that only captures a single point in time and thus cannot distinguish asymptomatic from pre-symptomatic infections.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the limitations of single-timepoint sampling.

claim: Repeated sampling over time could unambiguously identify asymptomatic infections.
source: In principle, repeated sampling over time could unambiguously identify asymptomatic infections.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the advantages of longitudinal sampling.

claim: Recent human infection trials have demonstrated a gradual 'fade-in/fade-out' sequence of qPCR signal intensity across the arc of infection.
source: Indeed, recent human infection trials have borne out this scenario (Chilengi et al., 2020; DeVincenzo et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published human infection trials.

claim: Cross-sectional observations lack the historical context necessary to trace the arc of infection.
source: By sampling a single point in time, however, cross-sectional observations lack the historical context necessary to trace this arc of infection.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the limitations of cross-sectional sampling.

claim: An IS481 CT <35 has been used as a diagnostic threshold of pertussis.
source: For example, an IS481 CT <35 has been used as a diagnostic threshold of pertussis (Tatti et al., 2011; Tatti et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature describing diagnostic criteria.

claim: Applying diagnostic thresholds to qPCR CT values introduces problems including calibration issues and a poorly examined trade-off between sensitivity and specificity.
source: This process introduces several problems, including calibration (e.g., between labs, machines, or over time) and a poorly examined trade-off between sensitivity and specificity that may also be task-dependent (e.g., clinical diagnosis).
evidence: This is an inference based on knowledge of qPCR methodology and diagnostic testing principles.

claim: Thresholding qPCR results discards information about signal intensity.
source: Further, this process discards information about qPCR signal intensity, such that borderline or low-intensity signals are summarily discounted as false positives or 'indeterminate'.
evidence: This is a logical inference about what happens when continuous data is dichotomized.

claim: Between April and November 2015, 1981 healthy Zambian mother/infant pairs were enrolled in the study.
source: Between April and November 2015, we enrolled 1981 healthy Zambian mother/infant pairs (3962 individuals) shortly after birth
evidence: This is directly stated and represents data from the study enrollment.

claim: Participants were observed during six clinic visits scheduled at roughly 2–3 week intervals through approximately 14 weeks of age.
source: and observed them during an additional six clinic visits scheduled at roughly 2–3 week intervals through approximately 14 weeks of age (when the last of the three routine infant DTP vaccine visits occurs).
evidence: This is directly stated and describes the study design.

claim: Of the initial cohort of 1981 pairs, 1497 mother/infant pairs attended at least one post-enrollment clinic visit.
source: Of the initial cohort of 1981 pairs, 1497 mother/infant pairs attended at least one post-enrollment clinic visit, and 834 pairs attended all seven scheduled visits (including enrollment, Table 1).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Table 1.

claim: 834 pairs attended all seven scheduled visits including enrollment.
source: Of the initial cohort of 1981 pairs, 1497 mother/infant pairs attended at least one post-enrollment clinic visit, and 834 pairs attended all seven scheduled visits (including enrollment, Table 1).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Table 1.

claim: The analysis focused on 1320 pairs with ≥4 NP samples per subject.
source: In this analysis, we focus on the 1320 pairs with ≥4 NP samples per subject (Figure 1).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 1 and Table 1.

claim: Infants were enrolled at a median of 7 days post-partum.
source: Infants were enrolled at a median of 7 days post-partum
evidence: This is directly stated as a demographic characteristic of the cohort.

claim: 47% of enrolled infants were female.
source: 47% were female
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Table 2.

claim: The median gestational age of enrolled infants was 40 weeks.
source: with a median gestational age of 40 weeks
evidence: This is directly stated as a demographic characteristic.

claim: The median birth weight of enrolled infants was 3000 g.
source: and birth weight of 3000 g.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Table 2.

claim: The median age of mothers was 25 years.
source: Mothers' median age was 25 years
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Table 2.

claim: Over 90% of mothers were married.
source: >90% were married
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Table 2.

claim: 17.5% of mothers were known to be infected with HIV.
source: and 17.5% were known to be infected with HIV.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Table 2.

claim: Nearly all HIV-positive mothers were on antiretroviral therapy at the time of enrollment.
source: Among the HIV-positive mothers, nearly all were on antiretroviral therapy (ART) at the time of enrollment
evidence: This is directly stated as a characteristic of the HIV-positive subset.

claim: Half of HIV-positive mothers had initiated ART prior to conception.
source: and half had initiated ART prior to conception.
evidence: This is directly stated as a characteristic of the HIV-positive subset.

claim: Nearly all mothers received at least one dose of tetanus toxoid during pregnancy.
source: Nearly all mothers received at least one dose of tetanus toxoid during pregnancy, signaling that some antenatal care was received by at least 99.5% of the maternal cohort.
evidence: This is directly stated as evidence of antenatal care.

claim: At least 99.5% of the maternal cohort received some antenatal care.
source: Nearly all mothers received at least one dose of tetanus toxoid during pregnancy, signaling that some antenatal care was received by at least 99.5% of the maternal cohort.
evidence: This is inferred from tetanus toxoid vaccination data.

claim: The final HIV status of the exposed infants could not be assessed.
source: The final HIV status of the exposed infants could not be assessed.
evidence: This is directly stated as a limitation of the study.

claim: Seven of eight mothers of symptomatic infants with definitive pertussis had at least one detecting IS481 assay.
source: Of particular note, seven of these eight mothers had at least one detecting assay, while six had multiple detections.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 2.

claim: Six of eight mothers of symptomatic infants with definitive pertussis had multiple IS481 detections.
source: Of particular note, seven of these eight mothers had at least one detecting assay, while six had multiple detections.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 2.

claim: Many mothers' detecting assays showed relatively weak signals (IS481 CT >40).
source: However, many of these mothers' detecting assays showed relatively weak signals (IS481 CT >40, e.g., mothers A, C, and H)
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 2.

claim: Only a few mothers' results met CDC's recommended diagnostic criteria for a positive test.
source: with only a few results meeting CDC's recommended diagnostic criteria for a positive test (Lievano et al., 2002).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 2 and citation to CDC criteria.

claim: CDC criteria were designed for application by clinicians when evaluating patients with severe and/or classic pertussis symptoms.
source: We note, however, that CDC criteria were designed for application by clinicians when evaluating patients with severe and/or classic pertussis symptoms, and were intended to favor specificity over sensitivity.
evidence: This is stated based on knowledge of CDC diagnostic criteria and supported by citation.

claim: CDC criteria were intended to favor specificity over sensitivity.
source: We note, however, that CDC criteria were designed for application by clinicians when evaluating patients with severe and/or classic pertussis symptoms, and were intended to favor specificity over sensitivity.
evidence: This is stated based on knowledge of CDC diagnostic criteria.

claim: CDC criteria were not designed for surveillance of asymptomatic individuals.
source: They were not designed for surveillance of asymptomatic individuals.
evidence: This is an inference about the intended use of CDC diagnostic criteria.

claim: Weak qPCR signals frequently bracketed visits with definitive test results in all eight infants who met CDC criteria.
source: Moreover, in our data these weak qPCR signals frequently bracketed visits with definitive test results and were observed in all eight infants who met CDC criteria at one or more visit.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 2.

claim: Infant G provides a clear example of pertussis infection fade-in and fade-out, including ptxS1 confirmation and severe symptoms occurring after the observed IS481 signal peak.
source: A clear example of pertussis infection fade-in and fade-out is provided by infant G, including ptxS1 confirmation and severe symptoms that occur after the observed IS481 signal peak.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 2.

claim: A weak IS481 signal in infant G at age six weeks precedes the acute infection observed around age 8 weeks.
source: Remarkably, a weak (and asymptomatic) IS481 signal in infant G at age six weeks precedes the acute infection observed around age 8 weeks
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 2.

claim: A weak IS481 signal in mother G is observed before 4 weeks of infant age.
source: while a weak IS481 signal in mother G is observed even earlier, before 4 weeks of age.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 2.

claim: The sequence of IS481 signals in mother/infant pair G suggests the likely sequence of transmission events within this pair.
source: This example suggests the likely sequence of transmission events within this mother/infant pair and thus influenced our emerging conclusion that weaker IS481 signals should not be automatically discounted.
evidence: This is an inference based on the temporal pattern of IS481 detections shown in Figure 2.

claim: Mother H had seven of nine assays (78%) detect IS481, but none reached CT <35.
source: Mother H provides another illustrative example, where seven of nine assays (78%) detect IS481, but none reach the canonical diagnostic threshold of <35, and none had a detectable ptxS1 result.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 2 and Table 5.

claim: None of mother H's assays had a detectable ptxS1 result.
source: Mother H provides another illustrative example, where seven of nine assays (78%) detect IS481, but none reach the canonical diagnostic threshold of <35, and none had a detectable ptxS1 result.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 2.

claim: The probability that all seven detections in mother H were false positives is low a priori.
source: A priori, the probability that all these detections were false positives appears low.
evidence: This is an inference based on statistical reasoning about the likelihood of multiple false positives.

claim: In the context of an infected infant, the explanation that mother H's detections were false positives becomes even less likely.
source: In the context of an infected infant, this explanation becomes even less likely.
evidence: This is an inference based on epidemiological reasoning about transmission within pairs.

claim: The more parsimonious interpretation is that mother H's seven NP samples contained pertussis, albeit at a low density.
source: While low sample pathogen density could also reflect clinically uninformative variation in sample collection and processing, the more parsimonious interpretation is that these seven NP samples contained pertussis, albeit at a low density.
evidence: This is an inference based on the pattern of detections and epidemiological context.

claim: All infants in the initial analysis were selected based on their presentation of symptomatic pertussis.
source: While all infants in this first analysis were selected based on their presentation of symptomatic pertussis, several of their mothers presented with no respiratory symptoms at clinic visits.
evidence: This is directly stated as part of the study design for the initial eight pairs.

claim: Several mothers of symptomatic infants presented with no respiratory symptoms at clinic visits.
source: While all infants in this first analysis were selected based on their presentation of symptomatic pertussis, several of their mothers presented with no respiratory symptoms at clinic visits.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 2.

claim: Mothers G and H each had multiple detecting assays, strongly suggesting asymptomatic pertussis infections.
source: Of particular note are mothers G and H, each of whom had multiple detecting assays, strongly suggesting asymptomatic (or minimally symptomatic) pertussis infections.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combination of multiple IS481 detections and absence of symptoms, supported by Figure 2 and Table 5.

claim: None of 500 randomly selected NP samples from the maternal catalogue yielded detectable IS481.
source: Based on our initial results, we next assessed how frequent low-intensity signals were in our cohort by randomly selecting 500 NP samples from our catalogue of over 9000 maternal samples. None of these samples yielded detectable IS481.
evidence: This is directly stated as a result of a random sampling analysis.

claim: The probability that seven of eight mothers of infected infants had one or more detecting assays occurring by chance was <0.0001.
source: Applying the binomial theorem for an expected frequency of just under 1/500 (i.e., assuming that the next sample would have been detecting), the probability that seven of eight mothers of infected infants also had one or more detecting assays occurring by chance was <0.0001.
evidence: This is a statistical calculation based on the random sampling data.

claim: Random chance is unlikely to account for the high concordance of IS481 detections within mother/infant pairs.
source: We conclude that random chance is unlikely to account for the high concordance within these pairs, or for their evident tendency to coincide in time.
evidence: This is an inference based on the statistical analysis and observed patterns.

claim: Approximately 91% of all IS481 tests were non-detecting.
source: Approximately 91% of all tests were non-detecting (N.D.), with 1561 detecting assays, including 818 in mothers and 743 in infants.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Table 3.

claim: 1561 IS481 assays were detecting, including 818 in mothers and 743 in infants.
source: Approximately 91% of all tests were non-detecting (N.D.), with 1561 detecting assays, including 818 in mothers and 743 in infants.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Table 3.

claim: Only 0.11% of mother samples and 0.18% of infant samples had CT <35.
source: Only 0.11% and 0.18% of mother and infant samples, respectively, had CT <35 and would have been considered definitive positive samples
evidence: This is directly stated and can be calculated from Table 3.

claim: The mid- and low-intensity CT strata closely mirrored the highest intensity strata in both mothers and infants, with a peak in June and July.
source: Of particular note, we find that the mid- and low-intensity strata (e.g., 40≤CT<43 and 43≤CT) both closely mirrored the highest intensity strata (e.g., CT<40) in both mothers and infants, with a peak in June and July and a long tail of decline in September and October.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 3B.

claim: The peak in IS481 detections coincides with a cluster of very high intensity assays (CT<35) and definitive infant pertussis cases.
source: This peak also coincides with a cluster over very high intensity assays (CT<35) that we highlight as points, and a related cluster of definitive infant pertussis cases described in our published 2016 analysis (Gill et al., 2016).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 3B and citation to prior publication.

claim: The high- and mid-intensity CT strata are highly correlated (infants, ρ=0.68; mothers, ρ=0.71).
source: Overall, these two strata are highly correlated (infants, ρ=0.68; mothers, ρ=0.71), and they rise and fall in synchrony (maximum cross-correlation at lag=0).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 4.

claim: The high- and mid-intensity CT strata rise and fall in synchrony with maximum cross-correlation at lag=0.
source: Overall, these two strata are highly correlated (infants, ρ=0.68; mothers, ρ=0.71), and they rise and fall in synchrony (maximum cross-correlation at lag=0).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 4.

claim: The mid-intensity stratum detects a pertussis outbreak 2–3 weeks before the high-intensity stratum in April 2015 in both infants and mothers.
source: However, the mid-intensity stratum is more sensitive to low infection prevalence in both infants and mothers, revealing a pertussis outbreak in April 2015 2–3 weeks prior to the high-intensity strata.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 4.

claim: Cohort size alone cannot explain the temporal patterns in IS481 detections.
source: We note that cohort size alone cannot explain these results, as the cohort's size reached a steady state in June of 2015 that was sustained through the end of December 2015 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of detection patterns with cohort size over time, supported by Figure 3C.

claim: The temporal patterns in IS481 detections are consistent with a population-level 'fade-in/fade-out' dynamic.
source: Rather, these results are consistent with a population-level 'fade-in/fade-out' dynamic, where multiple overlapping signals from single individuals (e.g., Figure 3A) sum to create these curves.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed temporal patterns and individual-level data.

claim: The range of CT values appeared greater for infants than mothers, with twice as many infants having CT results below 35.
source: We note that the range of CT values appeared greater for infants than mothers, with twice as many with CT results below 35 (15 vs 8, RR 0.54 95% CI 0.2–1.3).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Table 3.

claim: During the study, infants received routine whole-cell pertussis vaccinations according to the Zambian schedule at approximately 6, 10, and 14 weeks of age.
source: During our study, infants received routine whole-cell pertussis (wP) vaccinations according to the Zambian schedule at approximately 6, 10, and 14 weeks of age (see also Gunning et al., 2020).
evidence: This is directly stated as part of the study design and supported by citation.

claim: There is a gradual increase in the percent of infant assays that are detecting with increasing infant age.
source: Here we see a gradual increase in the percent of infant assays that are detecting with increasing infant age, though no such pattern is evident in mothers.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 5B.

claim: No pattern of increasing IS481 detections with age is evident in mothers.
source: Here we see a gradual increase in the percent of infant assays that are detecting with increasing infant age, though no such pattern is evident in mothers.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 5B.

claim: The increase in IS481 detections in infants is interpreted as cumulative ongoing exposure to pertussis in the early weeks of life that achieves a steady state at ~age 8–10 weeks.
source: We interpret this increase in detections as cumulative ongoing exposure to pertussis in infants in the early weeks of life that achieves an steady state at ~age 8–10 weeks.
evidence: This is an interpretation/inference of the observed pattern in Figure 5B.

claim: There is no statistical evidence of an effect of prior vaccine dose beyond the correlated effect of infant age.
source: While it is tempting to ascribe the flattening of this prevalence curve as possible evidence for a vaccine effect, we find no statistical evidence of an effect of prior vaccine dose beyond the (correlated) effect of infant age (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is directly stated as a result of statistical analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The steady state of approximately 10% detecting assays reached by infants at age 8–10 weeks approximately equals that of mothers.
source: We also note that the steady state of approximately 10% detecting assays reached by infants at age 8–10 weeks approximately equals that of mothers.
evidence: This is directly stated and can be observed in Figure 5B.

claim: Pairwise transitions of IS481 CT values within individuals tend to cluster, with orderly transitions over time.
source: Consistent with our hypothesis, we find that pairwise transitions tend to be cluster, with orderly transitions over time.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 6.

claim: Transitions from detecting to detecting IS481 assays are much more common than expected by chance alone.
source: In particular, transitions from detecting to detecting are much more common than expected by chance alone (red, lower left)
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 6.

claim: Transitions from detecting to non-detecting IS481 assays are much less common than expected by chance.
source: while transitions from detecting to non-detecting are much less common (blue, right column) than expected.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 6.

claim: Full-range CT values contain epidemiologically relevant information consistent with an underlying biologic process.
source: These results again demonstrate that full-range CT values contain epidemiologically relevant information consistent with an underlying biologic process.
evidence: This is an inference based on the transition analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: Individuals with three or more detecting assays are categorized as having strong evidence for infection (EFI).
source: Under the premise that many false positives would be highly unlikely regardless of signal intensity, we categorize individuals with three or more detecting assays as having strong EFI, as well as other individual within this EFI range (dotted line, EFI≥0.52).
evidence: This is directly stated as a methodological decision and shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Individuals with intermediate evidence (0<EFI<0.52) are categorized as having weak EFI.
source: Individuals with intermediate evidence (0<EFI<0.52) are categorized as having weak EFI.
evidence: This is directly stated as a methodological decision.

claim: When infants have no EFI, the corresponding mothers' EFI is also likely to be absent.
source: We find that when infants have no EFI, the corresponding mothers' EFI is also likely to be absent.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 7D.

claim: When infants display strong EFI, evidence in mothers also tends to be strong.
source: Conversely, when infants display strong EFI, evidence in mothers also tends to be strong.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 7D.

claim: The association between EFI categories in mothers and infants is consistent when varying the threshold defining strong EFI.
source: We also repeat this analysis by varying the threshold defining a strong EFI score (using either two and four detecting assays, respectively), and find consistent results throughout (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The concordance of EFI within mother/infant pairs offers strong evidence of transmission within the pair.
source: While this analysis does not provide evidence of contemporaneous infection within pairs, these results offer strong evidence of transmission within the mother/infant pair.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed concordance patterns shown in Figure 7.

claim: 188 mothers and 177 infants met criteria for Strong EFI.
source: Focusing on those with the strongest molecular evidence for pertussis infections, we identified 188 mothers and 177 infants who met our criteria for a 'Strong EFI'.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Table 4.

source: Within these groups, 130/188 (69%) of mothers had no symptoms
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Table 4.

claim: Among mothers with Strong EFI, 55/188 (29%) had minimal symptoms.
source: 55/188 (29%) had minimal symptoms
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Table 4.

claim: Among mothers with Strong EFI, only 3/188 (1.6%) had moderate to severe symptoms.
source: and only 3/188 (1.6%) had moderate to severe symptoms.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Table 4.

claim: Among infants with Strong EFI, 41/177 (23%) were asymptomatic.
source: By contrast, infants were more likely to be symptomatic than the mothers, but only in relative terms with 41/177 (23%) asymptomatic
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Table 4.

claim: Among infants with Strong EFI, 95/177 (54%) were minimally symptomatic.
source: 95/177 (54%) minimally symptomatic
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Table 4.

claim: Among infants with Strong EFI, 41/177 (23%) had moderate to severe symptoms.
source: and 41/177 (23%) with moderate to severe symptoms.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Table 4.

claim: 77% of infants with strong molecular evidence of infection were asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic.
source: Stated another way, 77% of infants with strong molecular evidence of infection were asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic.
evidence: This is directly stated and can be calculated from Table 4 data.

claim: Only one infant presented with classic symptoms of whooping and paroxysmal cough.
source: Only one infant presented with classic symptoms of whooping and paroxysmal cough.
evidence: This is directly stated as an observation from the clinical data.

claim: Baseline host immune status is at least partially responsible for mediating the clinical outcome of pertussis infections.
source: Such results are consistent with the theory that baseline host immune status (stronger in mothers, weaker or absent in infants) is at least partially responsible for mediating the clinical outcome of pertussis infections.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed differences in symptom patterns between mothers and infants.

claim: Minimally or asymptomatic infections occur commonly among infants.
source: It also emphasizes that minimally or asymptomatic infections occur commonly among infants.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Table 4 data.

claim: There is a strong positive association between EFI and antibiotic use in both infants and mothers.
source: Finally, we observe a strong positive association between EFI and antibiotic use in both infants and mothers (Figure 8C–D).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 8C-D.

claim: Antibiotic use presumably serves as a proxy for symptoms at some prior time.
source: On the one hand, antibiotic use presumably serves as a proxy for symptoms at some prior time, since a clinician must have judged the individual sick enough to warrant treatment.
evidence: This is an inference about the meaning of antibiotic use in the clinical context.

claim: Antibiotic use has been shown to reduce the infectious dose of B. pertussis through effects on respiratory microbiota.
source: On the other hand, antibiotic use has been shown to reduce the infectious dose of B. pertussis through effects on respiratory microbiota (Zhang et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Amoxicillin accounted for the vast majority of antibiotics use in this study.
source: We also note that amoxicillin, which is not effective against B. pertussis but is a first-line therapy for empiric treatment of pneumonia, accounted for the vast majority of antibiotics use in this study.
evidence: This is directly stated as an observation from the study data.

claim: Amoxicillin is not effective against B. pertussis.
source: We also note that amoxicillin, which is not effective against B. pertussis but is a first-line therapy for empiric treatment of pneumonia, accounted for the vast majority of antibiotics use in this study.
evidence: This is stated based on established knowledge of antibiotic efficacy.

claim: Erythromycin is available in Zambia but is not part of the Integrated Management of Childhood Illness algorithm and is hence rarely used.
source: Erythromycin, which would be active against pertussis, is available in Zambia but is not part of the Integrated Management of Childhood Illness algorithm by which children are diagnosed with pneumonia, and hence rarely used.
evidence: This is stated based on knowledge of local clinical practice.

claim: The results call into question whether ineffective antibiotics have been commonly prescribed for mild pertussis cases in this population.
source: With the above in mind, our results call into question whether ineffective antibiotics have been commonly prescribed for mild pertussis cases in this (and possibly other) populations.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed association between EFI and antibiotic use combined with knowledge of antibiotic efficacy.

claim: Full-range IS481 CT values offer valuable epidemiological insights when viewed in the context of repeated nasopharyngeal sampling.
source: In this paper, we aim to accomplish two central goals. First, we aim to demonstrate that full-range IS481 CT values (and not just CT <35) offer valuable epidemiological insights, particularly when viewed in the context of repeated nasopharyngeal (NP) sampling of a prospective cohort of 1320 mother/infant pairs followed across the first 3 + months of life.

evidence: This is an inference about the potential impact of cross-reactivity.
